The results of this week's election in Israel show neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
nor his main rival, Gadi Isincott, secured the 61 seats needed for a majority in parliament.
The political parties must now negotiate to try to form a coalition in the Knesset.
If negotiations fail, a new election could be held early next year.
Venezuela's political opposition leader, Maria Karina Machado, says she believes the country's
advance toward democracy is irreversible.
NPR's Kari Khan reports on Machado's first public address since she returned to Venezuela.
Dressed in a white suit, her trademark color, Machado thanked President Trump for his support
and U.S.-backed plans to have elections, which she said would be in 2027.
The transition of democracy is irreversibly.
The Democratic transition is irreversible and will be peaceful, she said.
She criticized an opaque U.S.-brokered oil deal and said her return was successful unlike
previous attempts because, quote, "they didn't see it coming."
Machado is now a direct challenge to the U.S.-backed interim president, Delci Rodriguez, who made
her own speech one hour before Machado's.
Rodriguez announced elections were coming and dismissed the opposition leader's return
as a, quote, "show."
Kari Khan, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
The Justice Department has issued grand jury subpoenas to election workers in Los Angeles
County.
NPR's Jude Joffe Block reports on what appears to be the Trump administration's escalation
of a feud over California's voter rolls ahead of next week's midterm elections.
The Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder's Office confirmed it received grand jury subpoenas
last week.
It's unclear at this point whether the employees who were subpoenaed are the targets of the
criminal probe.
But federal prosecutors have warned California election officials they could be committing
a crime if they process ballots cast by non-citizens.
The Justice Department is trying to force California to set aside the ballots of people
federal officials say are likely non-citizens.
But a federal judge rejected that request this week.
The Justice Department has appealed.
The same judge also told federal prosecutors to stop threatening local officials.
Jude Joffe Block, NPR News.
Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola says she knew nothing about an alleged effort by
her campaign to recruit a candidate to her race in Alaska with the same name as Republican
incumbent Dan Sullivan.
She was speaking to voters in Juneau after The New York Times reported her campaign had
done so in an effort to confuse voters, resulting in retired schoolteacher Dan J. Sullivan appearing
on the ballot.
Alaska's governor has ordered a criminal investigation into Peltola's campaign.
This is NPR News.
The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating yesterday's mid-air collision
between two helicopters in Oregon.
It left three people dead near a small airport southwest of Portland.
These have identified those killed on the two aircraft as a pilot from Oregon, a flight
instructor from Texas, and a student pilot from the United Kingdom.
Federal regulators are asking more than a half dozen companies about how they use consumers'
personal data.
Those companies include retailers Walmart and Target, and the ride-hailing company Lyft,
as NPR's Alina Seljuk reports.
The Federal Trade Commission has sent letters to nine companies, major retailers, airlines
and consumer apps.
The agency says it wants to look under the hood of how these firms charge different shoppers
and pay different gig workers for the same products or services.
For example, do people see different prices based on whether they are a member of a loyalty
program?
Or do delivery drivers get different wages based on how many orders they previously declined
to deliver?
The companies the FTC is ordering to answer its questions are Walmart, Target, Delta, United,
JetBlue, Uber, Lyft, DoorDash and Instacart.
Alina Seljuk, NPR News.
In Wisconsin, public schools in Milwaukee are closed today as the city celebrates the Brewers'
first World Series championship.
Tens of thousands of people are expected to line the streets for a parade to be followed
by a rally and a festival.
The Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays in five games to win Major League Baseball's fall
classic.
I'm Dave Mattingly in Washington.
